newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks stroll to narrowly mixed end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks stroll to narrowly mixed end.

text.p: *Stocks end narrowly mixed, little direction after early dip, jobs data little impact. Volume 396.98 million, value A$877.85 million, 1,097 stocks traded, 328 steady, 325 up, 444 down.
A slow Australian share market ended barely changed on Thursday as the market drifted with little motivation or interest from traders.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 1.8 points lower at 2,452.6.
The March share index futures contract was steady at 2,452, a 0.6 point discount to the underlying index.
The market dipped sharply early after the Dow fell, quickly pruned those losses and by lunch had found its niche in a narrow four point trading band just below square.
"I suppose the bias was down but there wasn't much in it," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
"The banks were down early although National Australia Bank was the odd one out. It was probably overdone yesterday."
National Australia Bank recouped nearly all of its Wednesday losses, adding 20 cents to A$16.05. The other big banks ended much as the rest of the market, narrowly mixed.
Labour force data failed to have any serious impact.
"Unemployment was a little worse than the market expected and that helped the bonds but didn't do much for us really," said a Melbourne broker.

Results continued, with Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer gaining 13 cents to an intraday high of A$6.04 before easing to close just two cents higher at A$5.93 after its sharply higher first half net profit of A$273.6 million and forecasts of similar second half profit growth.

Pay TV operator Australis Media topped turnover lists with brokers saying speculation of rationalisation in the profit-scarce industry was sparking investor's interest. its shares closed three cents higher at 18.5 cents on heavy turnover of 22.98 million shares.
Gold miner Mt Leyshon Gold Mines jumped 23 cents to A$2.35 after St Barbara Mines said late on Wednesday it would offer 32 of its shares for every 10 Mt Leyshon shares.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trade saw moderate activity but with few features.
Total options traded 37,682 (33,256)
Turnover in March SAPI contracts totalled 7,471 (5,930)

In other local markets, Australian bonds rallied after a much weaker than expected labour force report, but the long end proved more restrained ahead of two sets of key U.S. data over the next two days. By 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.81 percent.
The Australian dollar ran into profit-taking after its recent run-up faltered for the moment at US$0.7960 resistance. A soft set of local jobs data also slowed the unit's run.
By 1.30 p.m. (0200 GMT), the local dollar had backtracked to US$0.7915/20 from an early US$0.7951/56 and US$0.7941/46 late here Wednesday.
